decision: The published Carayol and Casselman interfaces yield CL1 and CL2 for the actual weight-two primitive form and compatible r5/r3 system, without losing dyadic primes, nebentypus, wild conductor or monodromy.

nine_obligations.name: source_hypotheses
nine_obligations.required: Carayol: cuspidal automorphic representation over a totally real field with regular algebraic archimedean type; Casselman: irreducible admissible infinite-dimensional local representations.
nine_obligations.constructed: The constructed finite twist of the Pan form is replaced by its primitive weight-two newform f over Q; Pi_f is its unitary cuspidal representation.
nine_obligations.why_match: At infinity its type is D_(2,0), satisfying parity and k≥2. Q has odd degree one, so no extra discrete-series finite place is required. Local factors of a cuspidal GL2 representation are infinite-dimensional and generic.

nine_obligations.name: constructed_objects
nine_obligations.required: The source theorem must apply to the same actual representation and primitive form used in the height argument.
nine_obligations.constructed: rho_l=b^-1 a_sigma mu_sigma composed with sigma is the corrected four-dimensional representation; the B splitting gives r_l direct-sum r_l. Pan at 5 yields the form; the finite character is absorbed before taking primitive f of level N.
nine_obligations.why_match: The scalar correction and actual A remain fixed. No unrelated elliptic family, independently selected form at 3, or artificially enlarged oldform level is substituted.

nine_obligations.name: domain_index_coverage
nine_obligations.required: Every rational prime p must be covered with coefficient characteristic different from p, including 2,3,5 and primes with p² dividing N.
nine_obligations.constructed: Use r5 for p≠5 and r3 for p=5. All are realizations of the same primitive f.
nine_obligations.why_match: This covers every prime exactly where Carayol’s theorem applies. Theorem A has no dyadic exception; the exceptional dyadic restriction belongs to the weaker Theorem B. No theorem at p=l is invoked.

nine_obligations.name: transition_comparison_maps
nine_obligations.required: Transport modularity from the chosen 5-adic embedding to the 3-adic realization and identify Carayol’s representation.
nine_obligations.constructed: At good primes outside a finite set, half the trace of reduced mu_sigma composed with relative Frobenius, scaled by b(sigma)^-1 a_sigma, is one algebraic number independent of l. Enlarge the coefficient field to contain f’s coefficients and transport equalities to an embedding at 3.
nine_obligations.why_match: Injectivity of the embedding turns equality at 5 into an algebraic equality. Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt identify semisimplifications; the known irreducible r_l forces the matching two-dimensional representation itself to be irreducible. No reliance on Carayol’s unpublished Ribet remark is needed.

nine_obligations.name: identity_of_consumed_object
nine_obligations.required: The minimal primitive level must equal the conductor of the full local Galois/Weil–Deligne object, not an inertia semisimplification.
nine_obligations.constructed: Casselman gives a(Pi_f,p)=v_p(N); Carayol identifies the full local parameter with the realization of this same f.
nine_obligations.why_match: The Weil–Deligne monodromy operator is retained. Frobenius semisimplification of a parameter does not discard N. The equality concerns the actual r_l in the Tate convention and is CL2.

nine_obligations.name: coefficients_normalizations
nine_obligations.required: Match central character, reciprocity, duality, unramified twists and epsilon-factor conductors.
nine_obligations.constructed: Nebentypus is arbitrary of conductor dividing N. Casselman’s epsilon(a)^-1 equals epsilon(d) on Gamma0(N). Carayol uses geometric Frobenius and a contragredient plus unramified norm twist.
nine_obligations.why_match: The conductor is invariant under duality and unramified twisting. Use the same conductor-zero additive character on both epsilon-factor sides. A different additive character would give a common dimension-dependent shift, not a new level. Coefficient extensions preserve conductor.

nine_obligations.name: local_conditions
nine_obligations.required: Allow arbitrary local type, ramified nebentypus, dyadic wild inertia and nonzero monodromy.
nine_obligations.constructed: The actual r_l may have all these local behaviors; V13 invokes Theorem A and retains both tame and Swan contributions.
nine_obligations.why_match: No supercuspidal dyadic or special representation is removed. The rational weight-two trivial-nebentypus corollary in Carayol 0.8 is not used as a substitute for general Theorem A.

nine_obligations.name: exceptional_cases
nine_obligations.required: Avoid applying Pan at 3, using l=p, assuming squarefree N or trivial character, or erasing monodromy.
nine_obligations.constructed: The 3-adic form is obtained by trace transport; p=5 uses l=3; p=2 and p=3 use l=5; all level exponents are allowed.
nine_obligations.why_match: A special unramified Weil–Deligne parameter with rank-one N has conductor one, although its inertia-semisimple part has conductor zero. This sanity check distinguishes the object required by CL2.

nine_obligations.name: downstream_consumption
nine_obligations.required: Convert actual local conductor bounds into a bound on the primitive level N of the same f, then supply that N to the modular-Jacobian height argument.
nine_obligations.constructed: CL2 feeds LR5, N≤210^300 R², and the following LR6 calculation. The baseline also uses J1(N), whose level must be this primitive N.
nine_obligations.why_match: This review accepts the conductor/level identification, conditional on the actual modular compatible system. It does not independently certify the ramification bounds, Li/Shimura Jacobian realization, source geometry, Pan final publication match, or final RC/318 conclusion.
